QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_17

question.text: A distributor's valuation responsibility is to:

answer.text: Understand valuation methodology and limitations, explain them and relevant risk disclosures to investors, and escalate or materially disclose concerns where applicable

explanation.text: The Logic: Distributors are expected to understand AIF products, including the methodology and limitations of their valuation, educate investors on these limitations, explain relevant disclosures and risk factors, and protect investor interests. Where concerns arise, they should be escalated or materially disclosed as part of good-practice duties. The Trap: Ignoring valuation, guaranteeing NAV will only increase, or independently re-valuing the portfolio each fall outside the distributor's role and would either mislead investors or duplicate the work of the valuer. Note: Based on NISM Series XIX-A workbook pages 245, 268, 270, 271, 274, and 276, which set out distributor responsibilities around understanding products, explaining disclosures, and good-practice duties to investors.
